newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond issuance mounts, spreads widen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond issuance mounts, spreads widen.

text.p: A $1.5 billion wave of high-grade U.S. corporate bond issuance hit the market on Wednesday and pressured spreads to loosen moderately, dealers said.

Bank and finance issues continued to surface at a heady pace, and spreads were wider by two basis points on a broad basis. Still, dealers stressed deals were "getting done" and wider spreads did not signify underlying weakness.

In fact, deals were being upsized to meet carnivorous investor demand, dealers said. Lehman Brothers Holdings's $300 million Baa1/single-A 2003 notes, upped by $50 million, were priced to yield 7.318 percent or a spread of 88 basis points.

Moving on, Bayerische Landesbank New York issued $250 million two-year non-callable AAA/AAA rated deposit notes as 6s at par to yield nine basis points over Treasuries. The deal was managed by Salomon Brothers Inc.

Bank and finance issues priced on Tuesday received mixed demand on Wednesday, traders said. Bear Stearn & Co's $150 million 10-year senior notes were quoted little changed to wider at 74 basis point bid, 72 offer and PaineWebber Inc's $150 million 12-year non-callable notes were slightly tighter at 111 bid, 108 offer.
The PaineWebber notes were priced at 112.5 basis points.
Also priced on Wednesday was Allegiance Corp's $550 million three-tranche Baa3/BBB-minus issue via a Goldman Sachs & Co led group.

A $200 million tranche of 10-year notes was priced to yield 7.33 percent, or 78 basis points over Treasuries; a $150 million tranche of 20-year debentures was priced to yield 7.841 percent, or 98 basis points over Treasuries; and a $200 million tranche of 30-year debentures with a seven year put feature was priced to yield 7.013 percent, or 57 basis points over Treasuries.
PanEnergy Corp issued $150 million 10-year Baa2/BBB non-callable notes via Chase Securities Inc. The notes were priced as 7s to yield 7.106 percent, or 59 basis points over the Treasury curve.
Kohl's Corp issued $100 million non-callable Baa1/BBB notes due 2011 as 7-3/8s to yield 7.413 percent, or 90 basis points over the Treasury curve. The deal was led by Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.

The supply surge was, in part, blamed for late weakness in the U.S. Treasury market, according to analysts. Comments from Federal Reserve governor Lawrence Lindsey that suggested a temoporary rise in future interest rates may be used to curb inflation also weighed on the market, they said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond closed down 10/32 at 98-31/32 to yield 6.83 percent.

In spot corporate news, American Brands Inc's debt was expected to tighten after Tuesday's announcement the company will spin off its UK-based Gallaher tobacco business. Under the plan, American Brands will shift $1.4 billion of $1.7 billion outstanding debt to Gallaher.
"There are not a lot of issues and whoever's holding them will probably shake out in the next couple of days," one tobacco trader said, adding they will garner tight bids.

Turning to high-yield trade, traders said prices drifted in the third consecutive day of lackluster action. As on Tuesday, traders surmised investors were merely in "waiting mode" before fresh paper hits the market later this week.
Outdoor Systems' $250 million 10-year notes, priced at par on Tuesday, held their ground at par bid, 100-1/4 offer.
